graph.summary: Insulin → Insulin receptor → Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 4 (GLUT4) → glucose import → Hyperglycemia → Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus

evidence.snippet: The binding of insulin to the insulin receptor (IR) triggers a cascade of receptor conformational changes and autophosphorylation, leading to the activation of metabolic and mitogenic pathways.
evidence.explanation: Insulin binds the insulin receptor and triggers its autophosphorylation/activation.

paper.title: A stepwise activation model for the insulin receptor.

evidence.snippet: This insulin-induced redistribution of GLUT4 protein is achieved through a series of highly organized membrane trafficking events, orchestrated by insulin receptor signals.
evidence.explanation: Insulin receptor signals drive GLUT4 redistribution (translocation) to the plasma membrane.

paper.title: Insulin receptor signals regulating GLUT4 translocation and actin dynamics.

evidence.snippet: insulin-stimulated glucose uptake is dependent upon translocation of the insulin-responsive glucose transporter GLUT4 from intracellular storage compartments to the plasma membrane
evidence.explanation: GLUT4 at the plasma membrane mediates insulin-stimulated glucose uptake/import.

paper.title: Insulin receptor signals regulating GLUT4 translocation and actin dynamics.

evidence.snippet: The enhanced disposal of glucose by the peripheral tissue is an important mechanism to regulate hyperglycemia.
evidence.explanation: Enhanced glucose uptake/disposal by peripheral tissues reduces hyperglycemia.

paper.title: Glucose uptake stimulatory potential and antidiabetic activity of the Arnebin-1 from Arnabia nobelis.

evidence.snippet: This well-characterized T1D model develops insulin deficiency with chronic hyperglycemia
evidence.explanation: Chronic hyperglycemia is a defining feature of type 1 diabetes.

paper.title: In vivo Detection and Correlation of Cerebral Ketone Bodies with Neurotransmitters in Streptozotocin-Induced Type 1 Diabetic Rats.
